items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: Jimmy had these boys in to the theater every first show... They took a lot of our method of playing... Jimmy told me in front of all the boys... he said, 'You know, Sam, you was my inspiration.'

ctx.x: So now I was taken away from the piano. But we started -- Lyons said, 'Well, now we're going to do vaude-'

-ville, which we did. Being a Loew -- he was the Loew agent. So, naturally, the whole year that we were back, we did that. From Loew's, from place to place, place to place, we'd play and play and we'd come back to Loew's State about four times. We'd already played it once out of the Club Alabam. But, here's the point that followed us now was on account of being like that, why we couldn't, we didn't play any more dances, see? We was just playing vaudeville. We had one date that was worth mentioning. We played the…

He said, 'Anyhow.' But As thing come on. So we were working in vaudeville at the time and I got this cablegram from Europe to come to the Ufe Palace if I wanted to. And they said the money was good and we had a powow and that was about the same chance I had to go -- the Cotton Club was opening. So we all had a powow, and we decided to take the Ufe Palace, because the Cotton Club was just starting in Harlem and -some of them been born- we had all been born in Harlem and others been living there all their life, and…
